download.maps: a 1024 px JPEG colour map and two 1024 px PNG maps (normal and one more), an OpenPBR material

use: The snigilsteinn gift (surprise-items.js GIFT_ITEMS.ammonite): two instances, one on each of the pair's leaves, lying flat and leant toward the camera. +Y up, the origin on the ground in the middle of its footprint (feet on y = 0).

size.note: 1.7 m across, 0.66 m high; an ammonite of a few centimetres on a stone, shown about 30 times its size so a child sees it from the glade (a closed leaf is about 2.1 m across)

modifications: blender-gift.py: the two meshes (the stone and the ammonite, one material) joined, the seam vertices welded, decimated by collapse from 3,052 to 2,900 triangles, custom normals from the welded whole, scaled to 1.7 m and set on y = 0, the material rebuilt as plain metal-rough (colour map only, roughness 0.8), the colour map written as WebP at quality 80 at 512 px. quantize-glb.mjs: positions 16-bit, normals 8-bit, texture coordinates 16-bit.
